title: Server and Storage Fundamentals
subject: Server and storage
description: Server form factors, key components, storage types, RAID, backup and disaster recovery, and how to size and quote server and storage systems.

lessons.title: Server form factors and key components
lessons.body:
Servers come in several form factors:

- **Tower:** a standalone unit for small offices.
- **Rack:** mounted in a standard cabinet, common in server rooms and data centres.
- **Blade:** many compact servers sharing one chassis for power and cooling.

Key components are the processor (CPU), memory (RAM), storage, network interfaces, and power supplies. Redundant power supplies and fans keep a server running when one part fails. Sizing starts with the workloads each server must run.

lessons.title: Storage types: DAS, NAS, and SAN
lessons.body:
Storage is connected in different ways:

- **Direct-attached storage (DAS):** disks connected directly to one server. Simple, but not shared.
- **Network-attached storage (NAS):** a file-level storage device on the network, shared by many users. Common for file sharing.
- **Storage area network (SAN):** block-level storage on a dedicated network, used by servers for databases and virtual machines that need low latency.

Choose by how many systems must share the data and what performance they need.

lessons.title: RAID, backup, and disaster recovery
lessons.body:
RAID combines disks for performance or redundancy. RAID 1 mirrors data across two disks. RAID 5 and RAID 6 spread data and parity across disks, and survive one or two disk failures respectively.

RAID is not backup. A deleted file or a ransomware attack is copied across the RAID set. Backup keeps separate copies at defined points in time, and must be tested by restoring it. Disaster recovery adds a copy at another site, with a defined recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO).

lessons.title: Sizing and quoting
lessons.body:
Before quoting, confirm:

- The applications to run, their CPU and memory needs, and expected growth.
- Storage capacity needed now and in three to five years, and the growth rate.
- Backup and recovery requirements, including RTO and RPO.
- Power, cooling, and rack space available.
- Warranty and support levels required.

Quote the configuration with its warranty, support, and installation. A server quoted without a backup plan is an incomplete proposal.
